Using \(A \cdot C = C\), we get \(C(A-1)=0\), so either \(C=0\) or \(A=1\).

- If \(C=0\), then \(A B^2 = 10A\), so \(B^2=10\), impossible.
- If \(A=1\), then \(B^2 = 10 + C\). The only digit square between 10 and 19 is \(16\), so \(B=4\) and \(C=6\).

Thus the original number is \(144\).

\[
\boxed{144}
\]
